assertion_audit.failure_condition: A dry pass reporting itself as an applied one.
A dry pass unlinking an aged entry.
The sweep ceasing to judge or unlink entries past the age threshold, or its roots or glob ceasing to reach the store.
A cutoff that removes an entry written inside the window, i.e. an off-by-a-sign age comparison.
The report recording no removal, a different path, or an extra entry.
The removal no longer announced on stderr.
The announcement returning to stdout, which is what negative-control.log records reddening.
The negative control's mutation failing to disable the sweep, i.e. the pass reaching memos some other way.
The report listing memos when its roots were emptied, i.e. the roots not being the source of discovery.

assertion_independence: No input-echo assertion: each assertion compares the filesystem or the pass report against a path the test created before the call, so the sweep must have discovered and removed it. The one gap is the path convention itself, with the fixture at :27 constructing home/cache/kind/<digest>-v1.json rather than deriving it from metadata_index._persisted_cache_path, so agreement with the writer is assumed rather than asserted (finding recorded).

review_limitations: Read-only review: no mutation and no test re-run; gate, arm and negative-control results are read from the recorded logs.
The claim that a stdout announcement corrupted the JSON report is read from the caller code and the repair's own rationale, not observed on a live invocation.
The unbounded-kind finding rests on reading the other callers of _persisted_cache_path, not on measuring directory sizes.
